text: Toddler refused every single thing I offered for dinner and then ate a crayon. Parenting is a joke and I am the punchline.
Dad didn't recognise me today. He asked when his daughter was coming. I said soon.
Maya read a whole book to me tonight. Every word. Six months ago she couldn't read at all.
Third night of the baby screaming. I put her down safely and went into the garden for two minutes just to breathe.
Mum's carer didn't turn up again. Had to leave work early. My manager's patience is running out and so is mine.
The kids made breakfast in bed for my birthday. Burnt toast, cold tea, a drawing of me as a dinosaur. Perfect.
Respite carer is here for the weekend so I can sleep. Grateful doesn't cover it.
Leo's first day at nursery. He didn't look back once. I cried in the car for ten minutes.
Sat in the hospital car park after Dad's appointment and didn't move for half an hour. I don't know what I'm feeling.
School called. Jonah hit another child. He's never done that before. Meeting with the head on Friday.
Rare quiet evening. Kids asleep, Tom reading, me with a book and tea. Everything is fine.
I'm so angry at the council. Six months on the waiting list for Mum's stair lift and she fell again.
Ava rode her bike without stabilisers today! She screamed 'I'm flying!' all the way down the path.
I love my children and I am so, so tired. Both true. Every day.
Haven't had a conversation with an adult that wasn't about nappies in four days.
Grandma moved in with us. Small house, big hearts, very full bathroom schedule.
Our son got his autism diagnosis. Relief that we finally know. Fear about what comes next. Love that doesn't change.
Every night I lie awake wondering if I'm doing enough for Mum. Then I go and check she's breathing.
Twins both slept through the night for the first time ever. I woke up at 4 in a panic because it was quiet.
Rosie's teacher said she's 'a joy to have in class'. Framing it.
Can't remember the last time I did something just for me. Cancelled the haircut again.
Teenager slammed the door, said I 'ruin everything'. I made his favourite dinner anyway. He came down and said sorry.
Grateful to my sister for having the kids every Wednesday so I can do my course. She never complains.
Mum keeps asking for her husband. Dad died nine years ago. I tell her he's at work. It breaks me every time.
School holidays start tomorrow. Six weeks. I have planned nothing. Wish me luck.
Family day at the zoo. Ice cream, penguins, one tantrum. Overall a win.
Exhausted. Work, school run, Dad's tablets, dinner, bath, bedtime, laundry. Repeat.
Esme asked me tonight if Grandpa can see us from heaven. I said yes. Then I went and cried in the shower.
Dad laughed at a joke on the radio today. A proper laugh. First time since the stroke.
Got the call from the adoption agency: we're approved. Pacing round the kitchen like a lunatic.
Thomas got into the school we wanted. Relief everywhere. Opening the fizz.
Picking up toys for the hundredth time today. I am not a person, I am a tidying machine.
The carer, Joy, has been with Mum for two years now. She treats her like her own mother. I don't know how to thank her.
Kids at their dad's this weekend. House is too quiet. I keep walking into their rooms.
Watching Freddie sleep. His little fists. I'd do anything for this boy.
Parents' evening: every teacher said Isla is kind and works hard. Driving home I couldn't stop grinning.
I raised my voice at Mum today because she asked the same question six times. I'm ashamed. She's ill.
Ezra's fever finally broke. He asked for toast. Best word I've heard all week.
Hoping the new medication helps Dad's confusion. Doctor says give it a month.
Childcare costs went up again. Doing the sums at midnight. Maybe I'll have to drop to part time.
Tiny moment: Noah held my hand on the way to school without me asking. He's ten. That's rare now.
Mum passed in the night. Peacefully, the nurse said. I was holding her hand. I'm numb.
We finally sorted the bedtime routine. Bath, two books, one song, lights out. Peace in our time.
Hate the school WhatsApp group. Fifty messages about a missing PE sock.
Thinking about how my own mum did this with four of us and no help. I understand her so much better now.
Lily's recital tonight. She's been practising the same piece for months. I'm more nervous than she is.
Took Dad to the seaside like he used to take me. Pushed his wheelchair along the front. He held an ice cream and hummed.
Social worker visit went well. They're happy with how we're managing Gran's care at home.
Bit lonely being a stay-at-home dad. The baby groups are all mums and they're friendly but I'm always the odd one out.
Kids fought in the back seat for three hours. I sang loudly to drown them out. Arrived hoarse.
Sam took his first steps towards me in the kitchen. Four wobbly ones. Then sat down hard and laughed.
Too many people needing me at once: Mum's GP, the school, work, the boiler man. I hid in the loo for five minutes.
Anniversary of losing our first baby. Nobody else remembers. I lit a candle by the window.
Wrote down every funny thing the kids said this month. Reading it back made me laugh till I cried.
Grandad's 90th. Four generations round one table. He made a speech and forgot half of it. Nobody minded.
Ordinary school day. Drop-off, work, pick-up, pasta, bed.
I'm proud of how I handled Kian's meltdown in the supermarket. Stayed calm, knelt down, waited it out.
Seeing Mum in the care home is the right decision. I know it. It doesn't feel like it tonight.
Hoping this new school is kinder to Mira. First day Monday. Bought her the backpack with the foxes.
Partner took the kids camping so I've got the house to myself for two days. I don't know what to do with all this silence. Loving it.
Furious with the hospital. Discharged Dad at midnight in a taxi on his own. He's 88.
Found Ruby's first drawing of our family. I have three arms and a crown. Accurate.
Excited that Mum's coming home from rehab on Friday. Moved her bed downstairs. Bought her favourite biscuits.
Started thinking about what kind of parent I want to be, not just what kind I am on a bad day.
Grateful for the neighbour who brought round a lasagne when she saw the ambulance last night.
The night feeds are getting easier. Or I'm getting used to the zombie life. Either way.
I keep checking the baby monitor. She's fine. She's fine. She's fine.
Arlo won the spelling bee! Spelled 'rhythm' while I held my breath in the third row.
Wonderful, the school wants a costume for World Book Day tomorrow. Told us at 8pm. Love that.
Bathed Mum today. She held my hand afterwards and said 'my good girl'. I'll keep that one.
